test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: The Main Worker is a person who works for:

options.text: at least 183 days (or six months) in a year
at least 153 days (or five months) in a year
at least 120 days (or four months) in a year
at least 90 days (or three months) in a year

solution:
The correct answer is __**at least 183 days (or six months) in a year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Main Worker** in the Indian context is defined as a person who works for **at least 183 days**, which is approximately **six months**, in a year.
 
• This classification is significant as it is used during the national census and surveys to differentiate individuals who contribute significantly to the workforce from marginal or non-workers.
 
• The **183-day criterion** ensures that only those individuals who are primarily engaged in economic activities are categorized as Main Workers, avoiding the inclusion of occasional or marginal workers.
 
• Main Workers can be engaged in various sectors, such as **agriculture, industry, or services**, and may include both salaried employees and self-employed individuals.
 
• Those who work for less than 183 days in a year are categorized as **Marginal Workers**, indicating their limited participation in the workforce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Worker Classification in India:**

 
 
• The **Census of India** classifies workers into two categories: **Main Workers** and **Marginal Workers**.
 
• **Main Workers**: Those who have worked for the majority of the reference year (183 days or more).
 
• **Marginal Workers**: Those who have worked for less than 183 days in a year.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Worker Classification:**
 
 
• Helps in understanding the **economic participation** of the population.
 
• Used for formulating **employment policies** and labor welfare schemes.
 
• Provides insights into the **sectoral distribution** of workers across agriculture, industry, and services.
 
 
 
• **Marginal Worker Characteristics:**
 
 
• These individuals often engage in **seasonal or occasional work**.
 
• Many marginal workers are involved in **agriculture**, where employment is seasonal.
 
• Their contribution to the workforce, while significant, is often irregular and less stable compared to Main Workers.
 
 
 
• **Key Facts:**
 
 
• The classification of workers is essential for **economic planning** and understanding labor market trends.
 
• India's workforce distribution is highly skewed towards the **informal sector**, which includes a large number of Main and Marginal Workers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **183-Day Rule:** This rule is a standard for identifying Main Workers in India and reflects their consistent participation in economic activities.
 
• **Economic Contributions:** Main Workers are critical to sustaining sectors like agriculture, manufacturing, and services, contributing significantly to **GDP growth**.
 
• **Government Policies:** Worker classifications help in tailoring schemes like **MGNREGA** (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) to enhance employment opportunities.
 
• **Workforce Distribution:** As per the latest data, a significant portion of India's Main Workers is employed in the **agriculture sector**, followed by industries and services.
